story_description: Create the foundational data model and types for representing hook execution events in a timeline/Gantt chart format, enabling visualization of hook lifecycles with proper temporal relationships and hierarchical structure.
task_description: Define the core HookTimelineEvent struct and supporting enums (HookTimelineCategory, HookTimelineStatus) that represent individual hook execution events with start/end times, nesting depth, parent-child relationships, and execution status for Gantt visualization.
atom_description: Implement the HookTimelineEvent struct with UUID-based identification, name, category enum, start/end Date timestamps, depth integer for nesting level, recursive children array, and status enum. Also implement HookTimelineCategory enum with session/turn/tool/file/git cases and HookTimelineStatus enum with pending/running/completed/failed/cancelled cases.
problem_statement: The Hooks Builder currently displays hook executions in a flat list format without temporal context. Users cannot visualize when hooks started, how long they ran, which hooks ran concurrently, or understand parent-child relationships between session-level and tool-level hooks. A Gantt-style visualization requires a structured timeline event model that captures start time, duration, nesting depth, and hierarchical relationships.

assumptions: HookExecution model already exists in Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookExecution.swift with startedAt and completedAt Date properties
SwiftUI is available as the UI framework and Identifiable protocol is required for ForEach rendering
UUID is acceptable as the identifier type for timeline events
Date arithmetic for duration calculation uses standard Foundation APIs
Child events always have start times after or equal to parent start times
Maximum nesting depth is bounded by practical limits (typically 3-4 levels: session > turn > tool > file)
constraints: Must be a value type (struct) for SwiftUI state management and copy-on-write semantics
Must conform to Identifiable with UUID for stable ForEach identity
Recursive children array must not create reference cycles (struct ensures this)
Category colors are defined externally in theme constants, not hardcoded in model
All Date properties use system timezone, no UTC conversion required
Status transitions follow state machine rules: pending -> running -> completed/failed/cancelled
functional_requirements: FR1: HookTimelineEvent struct shall contain id (UUID), name (String), category (HookTimelineCategory), startTime (Date), endTime (Date?), depth (Int), children ([HookTimelineEvent]), status (HookTimelineStatus)
FR2: HookTimelineCategory enum shall define cases session, turn, tool, file, git each mapping to a semantic color role
FR3: HookTimelineStatus enum shall define cases pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled representing execution lifecycle states
FR4: HookTimelineEvent shall conform to Identifiable protocol using id property for SwiftUI compatibility
FR5: HookTimelineEvent shall provide duration computed property returning TimeInterval or nil if endTime is nil
FR6: HookTimelineEvent shall provide isActive computed property returning true if status is pending or running
FR7: HookTimelineEvent shall provide static factory method fromHookExecution(_ execution: HookExecution, depth: Int, children: [HookTimelineEvent]) returning HookTimelineEvent
FR8: HookTimelineCategory shall provide color computed property returning Color for visualization (referencing theme constants)
FR9: HookTimelineStatus shall provide iconName computed property returning SF Symbol name for status indicator
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Struct initialization shall complete in under 1 microsecond for single event creation
NFR2: Memory footprint per event shall not exceed 200 bytes excluding children array
NFR3: Children array should support up to 100 child events without performance degradation
NFR4: Duration calculation shall handle nil endTime gracefully without throwing
NFR5: Factory method shall validate input HookExecution and return nil for invalid data rather than crashing
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create new file HookTimelineEvent.swift in Blaze/Sources/Core/HookTimeline/ directory
Step 2: Define HookTimelineCategory enum with cases session, turn, tool, file, git and add color computed property returning Color from BlazeTheme
Step 3: Define HookTimelineStatus enum with cases pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled and add iconName computed property returning SF Symbol string

Step 4: Define HookTimelineEvent struct with all required stored properties: id (UUID with default UUID()), name (String), category (HookTimelineCategory), startTime (Date), endTime (Date?), depth (Int), children ([HookTimelineEvent]), status (HookTimelineStatus)
Step 5: Add Identifiable conformance (automatic via id property)
Step 6: Add Equatable and Hashable conformance using synthesized implementations
Step 7: Add duration computed property: var duration: TimeInterval? { guard let end = endTime else { return nil }; return end.timeIntervalSince(startTime) }
Step 8: Add isActive computed property: var isActive: Bool { status == .pending || status == .running }
Step 9: Add static factory method fromHookExecution that maps HookExecution.hookType to HookTimelineCategory and HookExecution.outcome to HookTimelineStatus
Step 10: Add documentation comments for all public types and members
Step 11: Write unit tests for all computed properties and factory method

api_contracts: HookTimelineEvent.init(id: UUID, name: String, category: HookTimelineCategory, startTime: Date, endTime: Date?, depth: Int, children: [HookTimelineEvent], status: HookTimelineStatus)
HookTimelineEvent.fromHookExecution(_ execution: HookExecution, depth: Int, children: [HookTimelineEvent]) -> HookTimelineEvent?
edge_cases: Edge case 1: endTime is nil for currently running hooks - duration returns nil, isActive returns true based on status
Edge case 2: startTime equals endTime for instant hooks - duration returns 0.0 which is valid
Edge case 3: Empty children array for leaf-level events - valid state, no special handling needed
Edge case 4: Deeply nested children (depth > 10) - no hard limit enforced, builder responsible for reasonable depth
Edge case 5: HookExecution with nil startedAt timestamp - factory method returns nil
Edge case 6: Unknown hook type in HookExecution - factory method maps to tool category as default
Edge case 7: Children array contains events with mismatched depth values - no validation at model level, builder responsibility
failure_modes: FM1: Factory method receives HookExecution with nil startedAt - returns nil, caller must handle optional
FM2: Duration calculation on event where endTime precedes startTime (clock skew) - returns negative TimeInterval which may confuse UI, recommend abs() wrapper in display layer
FM3: Memory pressure from very large children arrays - struct copy-on-write helps but recommend limiting children count in builder
FM4: Category color lookup fails if BlazeTheme not initialized - provide fallback Color.gray in color computed property
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Core/HookTimeline/HookTimelineEvent.swift and remove HookTimeline directory. No other files are modified. No migrations required as this is a new additive model with no persistence.

risks: Risk 1: Model design may not accommodate future requirements like cancellation reasons or retry counts
Risk 2: Recursive children array could cause stack overflow with extremely deep nesting
Risk 3: Category enum may need additional cases for future hook types
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Keep model minimal and extensible; add properties only when needed
Mitigation 2: Builder layer (G002) will enforce maximum depth limit of 10 levels
Mitigation 3: Use default case in switch statements to handle unknown future categories gracefully
